flows.title: PUT /v1/items/{itemId} – update item
flows.summary: The controller maps the request and calls ItemService inside a class-level transaction. The service rejects blank name/colour, loads the item through the Spring Data repository, updates and saves it. The controller turns each exception into a status code: 400, 404 or 500, otherwise 204.

nodes.label: PUT /v1/items/{itemId}
nodes.description: ItemController is a @RestController under /v1/items. It logs the request and delegates to the service, then maps outcomes to HTTP statuses.

nodes.description: The class is @Transactional, so the method runs in one transaction: the save commits when it returns, and a RuntimeException rolls it back.

nodes.label: ItemNotFoundException
nodes.description: Logged as an error and thrown; the controller turns it into 404.

nodes.label: set fields + save
nodes.description: Copies name and colour onto the entity and calls save, which updates the row.

nodes.label: 400 Bad Request
nodes.description: catch(InvalidItemException): logs the message and returns 400 with no body.

nodes.label: 500 Internal Server Error
nodes.description: Any other exception (for example a database failure) is logged and returned as 500.

notes: Validation is hand-written in the service; there is no @Valid on the request, and the id in the path is only checked by the database lookup.
The controller catches exceptions itself rather than using a @ControllerAdvice, so every endpoint repeats the same try/catch mapping.
Both exceptions extend RuntimeException, so @Transactional rolls back on them; nothing has been written before the validation or lookup, so there is nothing to undo.
